newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Fritz sees China boosting Asian growth.
newsitem.headline: Fritz sees China boosting Asian growth.

text.p: U.S.-based logistics and transportation group Fritz Companies Inc expects Asian revenues to rise by 25 percent a year over the next five years with China the biggest contributor, chairman Lynn Fritz said on Thursday.
"Year on year, we expect 25 percent per annum increases throughout Asia for the next five years easily," Lynn Fritz told a news conference.
"China is and will be the largest percentage contributor to Fritz's regional growth," he said.
The San Francisco-based freight transport group has more than 400 employess in major Chinese cities.
Asia currently accounts for 30 percent of its global revenue.
The Singapore operation was expectred to grow 30-40 percent growth over the next year, Fritz said.

Singapore contributes about three percent of Fritz's total revenue. For the nine months ended February 28, 1997, Fritz saw revenue at US$847.3 million against $783.6 million previously while net income fell to US$215,000 against $28.4 million previously.
Fritz, in Singapore to open a US$25 million regional distribution centre, said about 25 percent of the company's investments were in Asia.

The company, which includes among its customers high technology companies like Texas Instrument, Seagate, Xerox and Haliburton, expects increasing worldwide sourcing and distribution of goods to fuel growth.
"International sourcing continues to grow in a dramatic way and that will drive our growth," Fritz said.
The group had been on an acquisition binge the last few years and it now expects more organic growth from existing customers now that the mergers and acquisitions have been completed.
The company's 49 takeovers throughout the world in the past five years had dented earnings.
But Fritz was unfazed and said he was "confident the company will get back to normal earnings this year". He declined to give details.

The company sees 36-37 percent of its total revenue from its air freight operations, about 33 percent from ocean freight units, 25 percent from warehousing and distribution and the rest from information, consulting and insurance services.
